concerns.text: Two of the three concatenated datasets (davanstrien/authors_merged_model_prs, authors_merged_dataset_prs) are curated collections of PRs by model/dataset authors — i.e., the sampling frame itself is correlated with provenance. After concatenation, group membership (LLM vs Human) may be largely determined by dataset origin, so any 'associational difference' confounds provenance with dataset-source selection. The plan's mixed-effects model (Phase 4) uses only repo_name random intercepts + PR-level covariates; dataset/source is not included as a stratification or fixed effect, and no dataset-by-group cross-tab is reported. Add a source-dataset covariate/stratified analysis or report the group×source contingency table so readers can assess this confound.

Shapiro-Wilk at α=0.05 on large PR samples will reject trivially (normality tests are consistent), so test selection degenerates to Mann-Whitney U almost always — the 'automatic test selection' is effectively deterministic and the t-test branch is dead code at scale. Not invalid, but the plan should acknowledge this and pre-specify Mann-Whitney as the expected primary test, or use a robustness criterion (e.g., also report Welch t-test regardless) rather than presenting selection as data-driven.

FR-017 grounds issue-severity construct validity in 'Jones et al., 2022' — an unverified citation with no full reference. Per Constitution II this must be verified or removed; the plan/research docs already acknowledge the proxy limitation, so dropping or verifying the citation suffices.
